summary: Roger Heim was a scholar who studied at École Centrale Paris (~1920–1923) and the Science Faculty of Paris (until 1931). He held a post at the Muséum national d'histoire naturelle from circa 1929 to 1970.

Roger R. Jackson is a Buddhist studies and Tibetology scholar. He earned his B.A. from Wesleyan University and an M.A. and Ph.D. from the University of Wisconsin-Madison, later holding posts at Fairfield University and Carleton College.

Roger T. Ames is a philosopher and sinologist who studied at the University of British Columbia, National Taiwan University, and SOAS under D. C. Lau. He served as Professor of Philosophy at the University of Hawaiʻi (~1978–2016).

Roland Barthes was a French philosopher and linguist. Educated at Lycée Montaigne, Collège Louis-le-Grand, and the Faculty of Arts of Paris under Émile Benveniste, he held posts at CNRS (~1952–1959), EHESS (~1962–1976), and the Collège de France (1976–1980).
Roland Steiner is an Indologist and Tibetologist who studied under Michael Hahn. He held a post as Assistant Professor at the University of Marburg (attested 2002).

Roland Wenzlhuemer is a historian who completed his doctorate at the University of Salzburg and habilitation at Heidelberg. He worked at ZMO and the University of Berlin, before professorships at the University of Heidelberg and the University of Munich.

Rolf Alfred Stein was a Tibetologist and sinologist who studied at INALCO and EPHE under scholars including Granet and Pelliot. He held posts at INALCO (1949–1951), EPHE (1951–1975), and Collège de France (1965–1982).

Rolf Scheuermann is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He earned a Magister der Philosophie from the University of Vienna under the supervision of Helmut Tauscher and also studied under Khenpo Chödrak Tenphel.

Romila Thapar is an Indian historian and Indologist. She earned degrees from Panjab University and SOAS under Arthur Llewellyn Basham, and held major posts at Kurukshetra University, the University of Delhi, and Jawaharlal Nehru University (1970–1991).
Ron Garry is a scholar in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied under traditional teachers Lama Tharchin Rinpoche and Tulku Thubten Rinpoche.
Ron Leifer was a scholar in Buddhist studies who studied under Agehananda Bharati in 1964 and under the traditional teacher Khenpo Karthar Rinpoche.

Ronald D. Schwartz is a Tibetology and sociology scholar. In 1998, he was attested as Professor of Sociology at Memorial University of Newfoundland and an Honorary Research Fellow at the University of Hong Kong.

Ronald E. Purser is an academic in religious studies, philosophy, and management who studied under Koshin Ogui. He held a post at Loyola University Chicago (~1989–1997) before joining San Francisco State University circa 1997.

Ronald Egan is a sinologist who received his Ph.D. from Harvard University. He held academic posts at Harvard, Wellesley College, the University of California, Santa Barbara (~1991–2012), and Stanford University (~2012).

Ronald Eric Emmerick was an Iranian, Central Asian, Indology, and Tibetology scholar. After studying at Oxford under Harold Walter Bailey, he served as Lecturer at SOAS (~1964–1971) and Professor at the University of Hamburg (1971–2001).
Ronald M. Davidson is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and Indology. He earned his PhD at the University of California, Berkeley in 1985 and held a teaching post at Fairfield University.

Ronald Neufeldt is a scholar of religious studies and Indology. He held an academic post at the University of Calgary from circa 1977 to 2007, serving as Associate Professor of Religious Studies between ~1981 and 1989.

Ronald Y. Nakasone is a Buddhist studies scholar who earned his PhD from the University of Wisconsin-Madison (~1974–1980). He held posts at the Institute of Buddhist Studies (from ~1987) and Pacific School of Religion.

Rong Geng was a Chinese scholar of sinology, history, archaeology, and linguistics. He studied at Peking University from circa 1922 to 1926 and held a post at Yenching University between ~1926 and 1941.

Rong Ma is a sociologist and Tibetologist who earned a doctorate in social geography from Brown University. He served as Director of the Institute of Sociology and Anthropology at Peking University and was a visiting scholar at Harvard.
